facility_roles.quote: The experimenters whirled previously created antiprotons around the CERN1 Low Energy Antiproton Ring (LEAR)

intervals.label: antihydrogen production run on LEAR
intervals.note: Production over "a period of three weeks" in September 1995 (CERN press release of 4 January 1996). End: LEAR "was closed in 1996" (CERN Courier, 17 August 2000); PS210's own last run date is not stated.
intervals.quote: In September 1995, Prof. Walter Oelert and an international team from Jülich IKP-KFA, Erlangen-Nuernberg University, GSI Darmstadt and Genoa University succeeded for the first time in synthesising atoms of antimatter from their constituent antiparticles.

intervals.label: completed
intervals.note: Completion is taken as the closure of LEAR; the collaboration's own end date is not stated.
intervals.quote: When CERN's low-energy antiproton ring (LEAR) was closed in 1996 after more than 10 years of operation

name: PS210
notes: Result summary paper: PS210 collaboration, Phys. Lett. B 368 (1996) 251 (doi 10.1016/0370-2693(96)00005-6); the abstract of that paper could not be retrieved verbatim, so the result claim quotes the collaboration's own 1997 summary abstract.

physics_goals.quote: The next step is to check whether anti hydrogen does indeed "work" just as well as ordinary hydrogen.
physics_goals.value: Produce antihydrogen atoms (antiproton plus positron) as a first step towards CPT tests with the anti-atom

summary.plain: The CERN experiment that in 1995 made the first atoms of antimatter: nine antihydrogen atoms created in antiproton collisions with xenon in a storage ring. They lasted about forty billionths of a second.
summary.technical: PS210 at LEAR: antiprotons circulating in LEAR passed through a xenon gas jet, and antihydrogen was produced in flight via electron-positron pair creation; the atoms were identified by a characteristic detector signature. Nine atoms reported in 1996; eleven including expected background in the later summary.
